 This Appeal, Coming On For Final Hearing, This
Day, Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice N S Sanjay Gowda
Oral Judgment
1. The claimant being aggrieved by the award of compensation of Rs.61,380/- is in appeal.

2. The claimant had approached the Tribunal with an application under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, 'the Act') contending that he has suffered injuries as a result of an accident which occurred on 09.04.2014.
3. In support of his case, the claimant had examined the doctor - PW-2, who had stated that the claimant had suffered 10% disability to the whole body.

However, the Tribunal has halved the said disability and has taken the disability of the claimant at 5%.
NC: 2024:KHC:50806 4.
In my view, since the doctor has assessed the whole body disability at 10%, the Tribunal ought not to have taken the whole body disability of the claimant at 5%.
Hence, the whole body disability of the claimant is assessed at 10%.

5. The Tribunal has proceeded to assess the income of the claimant at Rs.39,600/- per annum (Rs.3,300/- per month) based on the and the same cannot be found fault with.
6.
As the claimant was aged 29 years as on the date of accident, a multiplier of '18' would have to be applied as per II Schedule to the Act.

Hence, under Section 163A of the Act, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.71,280/- (Rs.39,600/- x '18' x 10%) as compensation towards loss of future income as against Rs.35,640/- (Rs.39,600/- x '18' x 5%) awarded by the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/-
towards pain and suffering; Rs.15,000/- towards NC: 2024:KHC:50806 medical expenses; and Rs.3,740/- towards loss of income during treatment and laid up period and in my view, the said sums are just and proper, which do not call for modification and are hence affirmed.
8. A sum of Rs.2,000/- awarded towards conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges by the Tribunal is disallowed, as the claim is one under Section 163-A of the Act.

9. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:
As

As awarded Sl. awarded Nature of Heads by this No. by the Court Tribunal (In Rs.) (In Rs.)
1. Pain and sufferings 5,000/- 5,000/-
2. Medical expenses 15,000/- 15,000/-
3. Loss of future income 35,640/- 71,280/-
Loss of income during the 4. treatment and laid up 3,740/- 3,740/-
period Conveyance, nourishment,
5. 2,000/- Nil attendant charges Total : 61,380/- 95,020/-
NC: 2024:KHC:50806 10.

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.95,020/- as against Rs.61,380/- along with interest at the rate of six per cent per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
11. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded with interest within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
12. On such deposit, the entire compensation along with interest shall be released in favour of the claimant on proper identification.
13. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
